summary: [WP-030 Code Review — PASS] All four Review Dimensions pass. The BookmarksPanelViewModel wiring is clean, the critical unsubscribe-before-dispose ordering constraint is met in both the DisposeSubViewModels() path and the LoadAsync re-entry guard path, and the AXAML binding pattern mirrors the established PlayerView pattern. Four targeted tests cover the key scenarios. No blocking issues found. Three non-blocking observations recorded below.

comments.note: MovieEditorViewModel.cs line 54: `_bookmarksPanelLogger` is declared `ILogger<BookmarksPanelViewModel>?` (nullable), but the full constructor always assigns it a non-null value at line 343 via `?? NullLogger<BookmarksPanelViewModel>.Instance`. The null-coalesce at the usage site (LoadAsync line 750) is therefore redundant in the full constructor path — harmless, but noisy. A cleaner approach: initialize the field in its declaration (`= NullLogger<BookmarksPanelViewModel>.Instance`), make it non-nullable, and drop the double null-coalesce. This eliminates the nullable annotation and the defensive double guard without changing behaviour.

LoadAsync disposal sequencing inconsistency: `DisposeSubViewModels()` is called conditionally inside the image-services guard block (line 675), yet that method also disposes PlayerVm and BookmarksPanelVm. When image services ARE present, the explicit re-entry guards at lines 719-721 (PlayerVm) and 735-740 (BookmarksPanelVm) become redundant no-ops. When image services are ABSENT, only the explicit guards operate. The behaviour is correct in both paths but the split logic is harder to reason about for future maintainers. Consider hoisting `DisposeSubViewModels()` to the top of `LoadAsync` (unconditionally) to normalize both paths and eliminate the conditional dependency.

No test verifies that `OnBookmarkSeekRequested` (MovieEditorViewModel.cs line 846) correctly forwards the `positionMs` argument to `PlayerVm.SeekCommand.Execute()`. The existing tests confirm panel creation, null-when-absent, dispose ordering, and re-entry replacement — but the actual seek-event forwarding path is only covered by code inspection. Adding a test that injects a fake PlayerViewModel with a spy SeekCommand and verifies the forwarded value would close this gap.

[documentation-forward] `DisposeSubViewModels()` docstring (line 793) lists all sub-VMs it disposes, but does not mention that this method is called conditionally from `LoadAsync` (inside the image-services guard) as well as from `Dispose()`. Future maintainers need that context to reason about disposal paths. Update the docstring to note both call sites.

[documentation-forward] The MovieEditorViewModel constructor now has 22 parameters. Both the implementation and QA pipelines flagged this as a known debt item (a dedicated `MovieEditorOptions` record would improve readability). Capture this as a named technical-debt entry in the project documentation / CHANGELOG so it is visible to future milestone planners.
